title: Activiti scenario file
description: Executable test scenarios for BPMN/DMN projects (docs/adr/0005-scenario-format.md, docs/user-guide/scenarios.md). One file holds the users, an optional fixed clock, any number of process scenarios and any number of decision cases. Executed by the activiti-scenario-runner library.

name.description: Name of the scenario file (shown in reports).

users.description: Users known to the identity store for this file. Key = user name, value = the groups the user belongs to (they become GROUP_<name> authorities; every user also gets ROLE_ACTIVITI_USER).

clock.description: Fixed engine clock applied before every scenario of this file (reset afterwards). A scenario may override it.

instant.description: ISO-8601 date-time with an offset or Z, e.g. 2030-01-01T09:00:00Z.

duration.description: ISO-8601 duration such as PT25H, P1D, P1Y2M3DT4H.

variables.description: Plain values (no matchers): they are sent to the engine.

expected.description: An expected value. A literal means 'equals' (numbers compare by value, dates by instant). An object whose keys all start with '$' is a matcher; any other object is compared key by key (exact key set); an array is compared element by element.

$exists.description: true: the key is present (even with a null value); false: it is absent.

$regex.description: Java regular expression; matches when it is found anywhere in the text of the value (anchor with ^ and $).

$contains.description: String: substring. Array: some element equals (or matches) the given value. Object: the given entries are present.

$size.description: Length of an array, object or string: a number or a matcher such as { "$gt": 1 }.

$any.description: The value equals or matches at least one alternative.

$ignore.description: The key must exist but its value is not checked.

start.description: How the root process instance of the scenario comes into being. Exactly one trigger: process (start by key), message (message start event), signal (signal start event) or timer (timer start event, together with its process).

process.description: Process definition key. With 'timer' it names the process that owns the start event; with 'signal' it narrows which new instance is the root.

message.description: Message name of a message start event.

signal.description: Signal name; the instance created by the signal start event is the root.

timer.description: Id of a timer start event; its start timer job is fired.

user.description: User that starts the instance (default: the built-in runner user).

expectFailure.description: The start itself must be rejected (for example a missing required variable); the scenario then has no steps and no expect.

step.description: One step: an object with exactly one key naming the step type.

taskMatch.description: Selects one task among several at the same activity (multi-instance). Every given field must match.

localVariables.description: Task-local variables the task must have (subset).

index.description: 1-based position among the matching tasks, ordered by creation.

expectTask.description: Asserts the open task(s) at a user task activity inside the scenario's instance tree. Reads the task through the engine TaskService (all tasks, regardless of who may see them); 'visibleTo'/'notVisibleTo' check visibility through TaskRuntime as the named users.

activity.description: Id of the user task element.

count.description: Number of open tasks at the activity; every field below is then checked on all of them (0: no open task).

candidateUsers.description: Exact set of candidate users (identity links of type candidate).

identityLinks.description: Identity links (TaskService.getIdentityLinksForTask) that must exist on the task, in addition to the candidates: for example the custom links of an activiti:customResource ({ "type": "supervisor", "user": "dave" }) or the links of the assignee (type assignee) and owner (type owner). Every listed link must be present; other links are not checked.

dueDate.description: ISO instant, null (no due date) or a matcher.

localVariables.description: The task-local variables: exact key set unless 'partial' is true.

partial.description: localVariables lists only some of the task-local variables.

visibleTo.description: Users that must see the task through TaskRuntime (assignee, owner, candidate user or member of a candidate group).

notVisibleTo.description: Users that must not see the task through TaskRuntime.

assignee.description: The new assignee (must be a candidate user of the task, per TaskRuntime.assign).

user.description: The current assignee, who performs the hand-over.

completeTask.description: Completes a task through TaskRuntime as 'user'. The user claims it first unless it is already assigned to that user. Variables are task-local and reach the process only through the element's output mappings.

expectFailure.description: The step must fail. Both fields are checked against the exception and its causes.

exception.description: Simple or fully qualified class name of the exception or one of its causes.

messageContains.description: Text contained in the message of the exception or one of its causes.

expectConnectorCall.description: Asserts on the recording wrapper around Connector beans: the calls made for a service task within the instance tree.

connector.description: Expected implementation (connector bean name), e.g. crm.LOOKUP.

count.description: Number of calls made so far for the activity.

call.description: Which call (1-based, in call order) 'inbound' and 'outbound' apply to.

inbound.description: Inbound variables of the call: exact key set unless 'partial'. Use { "$ignore": true } for keys whose value does not matter.

outbound.description: Outbound variables the connector returned: exact key set unless 'partial'.

path.description: Assertions on what a process instance did, read from its history and the recorded sequence flows.

order.description: Happens-before pairs [a, b]: a was entered before b (meaningful along one branch only).

notSequenceFlows.description: Sequence flows that were not taken.

expectChildInstance.description: Asserts on the child process instance started by a call activity of the scenario's tree.

callActivity.description: Id of the call activity in the parent.

process.description: Process definition key of the child.

count.description: Number of child instances the call activity has started (multi-instance call activities start several).

call.description: Which child (1-based, in start order) the following fields apply to.

startVariables.description: First recorded value of each listed variable (what the child was started with, after input mapping); subset.

variables.description: Current (or final) process variables of the child; subset.

messageStep.description: ProcessRuntime.receive: delivers a message to the single subscription with this name and correlation key.

signalStep.description: ProcessRuntime.signal: broadcasts a signal to every waiting instance.

triggerReceiveTask.description: RuntimeService.trigger on the execution waiting at a receive task (ProcessRuntime has no API for it).

match.description: Selects one execution among several waiting at the activity (a multi-instance receive task).

localVariables.description: Variables the execution must see (subset), such as the element variable of its instance.

expectTimer.description: Asserts on the timer jobs (not yet fired) at a timer event of the instance tree, read through ManagementService.createTimerJobQuery. The due date is the one the engine computed from the timer definition and the engine clock, so a fixed clock makes it exact.

activity.description: Id of the timer event (boundary or intermediate catch event); a timer job of a failed async job counts for its activity too.

count.description: Number of timer jobs at the activity (0: none). Default: at least one.

dueDate.description: Due date of the earliest timer job at the activity: an ISO instant or a matcher.

fireTimer.description: Makes the timer job of a timer event due now: moveTimerToExecutableJob, then executeJob (MANUAL) or wait for the async executor (EXECUTOR).

activity.description: Id of the timer event (boundary, intermediate catch or start event).

all.description: Fire every timer job at the activity instead of the earliest one.

executeJobs.description: Runs the due work of the instance tree: timers whose due date has passed on the engine clock, then executable (async) jobs, until none are left.

timeoutMs.description: EXECUTOR mode: how long to wait for the async executor.

failJobUntilDeadLetter.description: Executes the job at an activity again and again (moving retry timers to executable) until it lands in the dead-letter table. The job must keep failing.

expectActive.description: Activities that are currently active (RuntimeService.getActiveActivityIds, over the instance tree). An array means exactly this set.

state.description: COMPLETED: the root instance has ended. ACTIVE: it is still running and has no dead-letter job. DEADLETTER: it is still running and has at least one dead-letter job.

endEvents.description: Exact set of end events the root instance reached.

variables.description: Process variables of the root instance (subset). Read from history, so it works after the instance has ended.

deadLetterJobs.description: Exactly these dead-letter jobs exist in the instance tree.

decisionCase.description: Evaluates a DMN decision through the DecisionEvaluator and checks the result rows and matched rules.

decision.description: Decision id (or table name) to evaluate.

result.description: Result rows, in order. A single-result decision yields one row. Each row: exact key set.

matchedRules.description: Ids of the matched rules (order-free, exact set).
